l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The Nephites fought to defend their freedom and country, restored Pahoran, captured Nephihah, and drove the Lamanites from the land. After the wars, they reestablished the church and law, prospered, multiplied, grew strong and rich, and humbled themselves before the Lord.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The Lamanites were defeated in several encounters, lost the city of Nephihah, and fled into the land of Moroni before being driven from the land. Many prisoners entered a covenant not to fight the Nephites and joined the people of Ammon.

l: armies of the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni's army gathered additional men under the standard of liberty, united with Pahoran's forces, and became stronger than the men of Pachus. It captured Nephihah by lowering men over the wall with cords and ladders and later pursued and defeated the Lamanites.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The land of Zarahemla was taken by Pachus and his dissenters, then recovered by Moroni and Pahoran. Peace was restored there, and a large body of men was left to defend it.

l: city of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni and Pahoran went against the city of Zarahemla and defeated the men of Pachus there. Pahoran was restored to the judgment-seat after the city was recovered.

l: land of Nephihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni and Pahoran marched toward the land of Nephihah and fought and captured a large body of Lamanites on the way. After taking the city of Nephihah, Moroni marched from that land toward the land of Lehi.

l: city of Nephihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni's army entered the city of Nephihah by night using strong cords and ladders. The Lamanites fled, and Moroni and Pahoran obtained possession of the city without losing one soul.

l: judgment-seat, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The judgment-seat was taken from Pahoran by Pachus and his men. After Pachus was slain, Pahoran was restored to the judgment-seat and later returned to it after the wars.

l: liberty, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni raised the standard of liberty wherever he went, and thousands gathered to it and took up their swords in defense of their freedom.

l: freedom, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The people took up arms to defend their freedom and avoid bondage. Those who denied their freedom or fought against it were executed according to the law.

l: cause of their country, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Moroni rejoiced that Pahoran was faithful to the cause of his country. Teancum was described as a true friend to liberty who had fought valiantly for his country.

l: law, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The law was enforced against Pachus's men and the king-men who fought against their country or refused to defend it. Regulations were later made concerning the law, and judges and chief judges were chosen.

l: church of God, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Helaman and his brethren preached with power, causing many to repent and be baptized. They established the church of God again throughout the land.

l: thirty and first year of the reign of the judges, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The thirty and first year included the capture of Nephihah, the death of Teancum, and the defeat and expulsion of the Lamanites. It ended with peace once more established among the people of Nephi.

l: war between the Nephites and the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The war between the Nephites and the Lamanites had caused many years of wars, bloodshed, famine, affliction, murders, contentions, dissensions, and iniquity. Its length hardened some people and softened others, and it ended with the Lamanites driven from the land.

l: restoration of Pahoran to the judgment-seat, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The restoration of Pahoran to the judgment-seat occurred after Moroni and Pahoran defeated Pachus, slew him, and took his men prisoner.

l: capture of the city of Nephihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The capture of the city of Nephihah was accomplished at night when Moroni's men climbed over the wall with cords and ladders. The Lamanites fled, and the city was taken without the loss of one Nephite.

l: death of Teancum, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: The death of Teancum occurred after he entered the Lamanite camp and wounded Ammoron. Ammoron's servants pursued and slew him, causing Lehi and Moroni great sorrow.

l: peace in the land of Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Peace in the land of Zarahemla was restored by Moroni and Pahoran after they defeated Pachus and his dissenters. Later, the people of Nephi again prospered and strengthened themselves in the land.

l: Helaman's death, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 62
s: Helaman's death occurred in the thirty and fifth year of the reign of the judges over the people of Nephi, after the church of God had been reestablished and the people had begun to prosper.

l: The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Shiblon took possession of the sacred things from Helaman and later conferred them upon Helaman, the son of Helaman, before his death. Moroni died, and later Shiblon died while Corianton had gone to the land northward with provisions. Hagoth built ships that carried many Nephites, with provisions, women, and children, toward the land northward, though some ships were never heard from again. Dissenters stirred the Lamanites to war against Moronihah’s army, but the Lamanites were defeated and driven back to their own lands, and the account of Alma, Helaman, and Shiblon ended.

l: Shiblon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Shiblon took possession of the sacred things delivered to Helaman. He was described as just and upright before God, and he conferred the sacred things upon Helaman, the son of Helaman, before his death. Shiblon then died in the thirty-ninth year.

l: Helaman, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Helaman received the sacred things from Shiblon. The engravings in his possession were written and sent throughout the land, except for the parts Alma had commanded not to go forth.

l: Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Moroni died at the end of the thirty-sixth year of the reign of the judges.

l: Hagoth, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Hagoth was an exceedingly curious man who built an exceedingly large ship on the borders of Bountiful, by Desolation, and launched it into the west sea.

l: Corianton, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Corianton had gone forth to the land northward in a ship to carry provisions to the people who had gone there.

l: Moronihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Moronihah led the people or army against whom the Lamanites came to war. His army defeated and drove the Lamanites back to their own lands.

l: Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Many Nephites entered Hagoth’s ships with provisions, women, and children and sailed toward the land northward. Many people also went forth into the land northward in the thirty-eighth year.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The Lamanites were stirred up by dissenters and came down with a numerous army against Moronihah’s army. They were beaten, driven back to their own lands, and suffered great loss.

l: company of men, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: A company of five thousand four hundred men, with their wives and children, departed from Zarahemla into the land northward.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Zarahemla was the land from which a company of men, with their wives and children, departed for the land northward.

l: land northward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The land northward received a company of men and many other people from Zarahemla. Corianton went there by ship to carry provisions, and several voyages were directed there.

l: Bountiful, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Bountiful was where Hagoth built his exceedingly large ship, on its borders by Desolation.

l: land Desolation, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Desolation was located by Bountiful, near the place where Hagoth built his exceedingly large ship.

l: sacred things, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The sacred things were delivered from Helaman to Shiblon and later conferred by Shiblon upon Helaman, the son of Helaman, before Shiblon died. They were to be kept sacred and handed down from one generation to another.

l: engravings, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The engravings in Helaman’s possession were written and sent throughout the land among the children of men, except for the parts Alma had commanded not to go forth.

l: ships, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Hagoth built an exceedingly large ship and later built other ships. The first ship returned and sailed again with more people and provisions, while another ship also sailed forth; some ships were never heard from again.

l: army of Moronihah, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The army of Moronihah fought the Lamanites and defeated them, driving them back to their own lands with great loss.

l: migration to the land northward, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: A company of five thousand four hundred men, with their wives and children, migrated from Zarahemla to the land northward. Many other people also went forth into that land in later years.

l: voyages of Hagoth's ships, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Hagoth’s ships carried Nephites, provisions, women, and children toward the land northward. The first ship returned and sailed again, while other ships sailed forth and were never heard from or had an unknown destination.

l: death of Moroni, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Moroni died at the end of the thirty-sixth year of the reign of the judges.

l: death of Shiblon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Shiblon died in the thirty-ninth year after conferring the sacred things upon Helaman, the son of Helaman.

l: war against the Nephites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: Dissenters went to the Lamanites and stirred them up against the Nephites. The Lamanites came with a numerous army to war against Moronihah’s army.

l: defeat and retreat of the Lamanites, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The Lamanites were beaten by Moronihah’s army and driven back to their own lands, suffering great loss.

l: account of Alma, Helaman, and Shiblon, The Book of Alma, the Son of Alma, Chapter 63
s: The account of Alma, Helaman his son, and Shiblon, who was his son, ended at the close of the thirty-ninth year of the reign of the judges.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The Book of Helaman concerns the Nephites, their wars, contentions, dissensions, and the prophecies of many holy prophets before the coming of Christ. It records the conversion of many of the Lamanites and the righteousness of the Lamanites. It also records the wickedness and abominations of the Nephites down to the coming of Christ.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The Book of Helaman is an account of the Nephites, their wars, contentions, dissensions, and the prophecies of many holy prophets. It also records the conversion and righteousness of many of the Lamanites and the wickedness and abominations of the Nephites down to the coming of Christ.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The Nephites are the subject of an account concerning their wars, contentions, and dissensions. They are also described as wicked and abominable down to the coming of Christ.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: Many of the Lamanites are converted. The Lamanites are described as righteous.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: Christ is the person whose coming marks the period down to which the records extend.

l: wars, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The wars of the Nephites are recorded in the Book of Helaman.

l: contentions, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The contentions of the Nephites are recorded in the Book of Helaman.

l: dissensions, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The dissensions of the Nephites are recorded in the Book of Helaman.

l: prophecies of many holy prophets, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The prophecies of many holy prophets before the coming of Christ are included in the records of Helaman and his sons.

l: the coming of Christ, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The coming of Christ is the point down to which the records of Helaman and his sons extend.

l: conversion of many of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The conversion of many of the Lamanites is recorded in the Book of Helaman.

l: righteousness of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The righteousness of the Lamanites is recorded in the Book of Helaman.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman
s: The wickedness and abominations of the Nephites are recorded in the Book of Helaman down to the coming of Christ.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: After Pahoran’s death, Pahoran, Paanchi, and Pacumeni contend over the judgment-seat, causing divisions among the people of Nephi. Pahoran is appointed chief judge, but Paanchi is condemned to death and Kishkumen murders Pahoran; Pacumeni then becomes chief judge before being killed by Coriantumr. Coriantumr leads a Lamanite invasion, captures the city of Zarahemla, and advances through the land, but Moronihah and Lehi surround the Lamanites, kill Coriantumr, and force their surrender. Moronihah retakes Zarahemla and permits the captured Lamanites to leave the land in peace.

l: Pahoran, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Pahoran dies at the beginning of the fortieth year, after which contention arises over who should hold the judgment-seat. He is appointed chief judge by the voice of the people, but Kishkumen murders him as he sits upon the judgment-seat.

l: Paanchi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Paanchi contends for the judgment-seat and becomes exceedingly angry when Pahoran is appointed. He is taken, tried, and condemned to death for raising a rebellion and seeking to destroy the liberty of the people.

l: Pacumeni, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Pacumeni cannot obtain the judgment-seat but unites with the voice of the people. He is appointed chief judge after Pahoran’s death and is later killed by Coriantumr against the wall of Zarahemla.

l: Kishkumen, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Kishkumen is sent by those who supported Paanchi to murder Pahoran. He escapes pursuit in disguise and covenants with his band to conceal the murder.

l: Coriantumr, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Coriantumr, a descendant of Zarahemla and a dissenter from the Nephites, leads the Lamanite army into the land of Zarahemla. He captures the city of Zarahemla, kills Pacumeni, advances toward Bountiful, and is killed when Moronihah surrounds the Lamanites.

l: Moronihah, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Moronihah has strong armies stationed around the borders because he expects the Lamanites to attack there. After Coriantumr invades the center of the land, Moronihah sends Lehi to head the army and later heads the retreat, surrounds the Lamanites, recaptures Zarahemla, and sends the prisoners out of the land in peace.

l: Lehi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Moronihah sends Lehi with an army to head Coriantumr’s forces before they reach the land of Bountiful. Lehi’s action causes the Lamanites to begin retreating toward Zarahemla.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The Nephites experience serious contention over the judgment-seat and fail to keep sufficient guards in Zarahemla. They suffer heavy losses during Coriantumr’s invasion but later surround the Lamanites, receive their surrender, and retake Zarahemla.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The Lamanites gather an innumerable army under Coriantumr and invade the center of the Nephite land. They capture Zarahemla and many cities, but after Coriantumr is killed they surrender to the Nephites and are allowed to leave in peace.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The people of Nephi divide into three groups over the competing claims of Pahoran, Paanchi, and Pacumeni. By their voice, they appoint Pahoran and later Pacumeni as chief judge and governor.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The land of Zarahemla is invaded by Coriantumr’s Lamanite army, which marches through its center and attacks its cities. Moronihah and the Nephites later drive the Lamanites back and regain control.

l: the great city of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The city of Zarahemla is captured by Coriantumr after the Lamanites quickly cut down its watch and enter the city. Moronihah later takes possession of the city again.

l: city of Bountiful, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Coriantumr marches toward the city of Bountiful with the intention of cutting through to obtain the north parts of the land. He is headed before reaching it.

l: land of Bountiful, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Coriantumr intends to march through the land toward Bountiful. Lehi heads the Lamanite army before it reaches the land of Bountiful.

l: judgment-seat, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The judgment-seat becomes the focus of contention among Pahoran, Paanchi, and Pacumeni. Pahoran is appointed to it, is murdered while sitting upon it, and is succeeded by Pacumeni.

l: government, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Serious contention and difficulty in the government prevent the Nephites from maintaining sufficient guards in the land of Zarahemla. This lack of preparation enables Coriantumr’s rapid invasion.

l: serious contention over the judgment-seat, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: After Pahoran’s death, Pahoran, Paanchi, and Pacumeni contend over who should hold the judgment-seat. The dispute divides the people into three groups and leads to Paanchi’s condemnation and Pahoran’s murder.

l: appointment of Pahoran as chief judge, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Pahoran is appointed by the voice of the people to be chief judge and governor over the people of Nephi. Pacumeni unites with this decision, while Paanchi and his supporters become angry.

l: murder of Pahoran, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Those who supported Paanchi send Kishkumen to the judgment-seat, where he murders Pahoran. Kishkumen escapes and conceals his involvement through a covenant with his band.

l: Coriantumr's invasion of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Coriantumr leads an innumerable Lamanite army into Zarahemla while the Nephites are unprepared. He cuts down the watch, captures the city, kills Pacumeni, and advances through the land before being stopped.

l: battle between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: The Nephites battle Coriantumr’s Lamanite army as it retreats toward Zarahemla. Moronihah and Lehi surround the Lamanites, and the fighting is exceedingly bloody, with many slain, including Coriantumr.

l: death of Pacumeni, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Pacumeni flees before Coriantumr to the walls of Zarahemla. Coriantumr strikes him against the wall, and Pacumeni dies.

l: death of Coriantumr, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: Coriantumr is killed during the battle after Moronihah heads the Lamanite retreat. His death occurs while the Lamanites are surrounded by the Nephites on every side.

l: Lamanite surrender, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: After Coriantumr is slain and retreat is impossible in any direction, the Lamanites yield themselves into the hands of the Nephites. Moronihah then causes the captured Lamanites to depart out of the land in peace.

l: Nephite recapture of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 1
s: After defeating and surrounding the Lamanite army, Moronihah takes possession of the city of Zarahemla again. The recapture ends the Lamanite occupation of the city.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Helaman, the son of Helaman, was appointed by the voice of the people to fill the judgment-seat after contention arose over who should hold it. Kishkumen, supported by his band and led by Gadianton, planned to murder Helaman as part of their secret work to murder, rob, and gain power. Helaman's servant learned of the plan through disguise, led Kishkumen toward the judgment-seat, stabbed him to death, and reported what happened to Helaman. Gadianton's band fled into the wilderness, and Gadianton was later identified as causing the overthrow and near-destruction of the people of Nephi.

l: Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Helaman, the son of Helaman, was appointed by the voice of the people to fill the judgment-seat. After Kishkumen was killed, Helaman sent to take the band of robbers and secret murderers so they could be executed according to the law.

l: Kishkumen, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Kishkumen had murdered Pahoran and planned to destroy Helaman, supported by his band. Helaman's servant led him toward the judgment-seat and stabbed him to the heart, killing him without a groan.

l: Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Gadianton was exceedingly expert in many words and in the craft of carrying on the secret work of murder and robbery. He became the leader of Kishkumen's band, promised its members power and authority, and later caused the overthrow and near-destruction of the people of Nephi.

l: servant (Helaman's servant), The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Helaman's servant obtained knowledge through disguise of the band's plans to destroy Helaman. He met Kishkumen, learned his purpose, led him toward the judgment-seat, stabbed him, and told Helaman what he had seen, heard, and done.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The Nephites had peace established again with the Lamanites by Moronihah. Among them, contention arose over who should fill the judgment-seat.

l: the people of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The people of Nephi had judges who ruled over them. The text says Gadianton later caused their overthrow, almost bringing about their entire destruction.

l: secret band of robbers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The band of Kishkumen had entered into a covenant that no one should know its wickedness. It sought murder, robbery, and power, fled into the wilderness after Kishkumen was killed, and could not be found by those sent to take it.

l: judgment-seat, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: There was initially no one to fill the judgment-seat, causing contention among the people. Helaman was appointed to it, and Kishkumen sought to reach it in order to murder him.

l: serious contention over the judgment-seat, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: After Moronihah had established peace between the Nephites and the Lamanites, contention began again among the people concerning who should fill the judgment-seat.

l: covenant of secrecy, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The band of Kishkumen had entered into a covenant that no one should know its wickedness.

l: secret work of murder and robbery, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Gadianton was exceedingly expert in the secret work of murder and robbery and became the leader of Kishkumen's band.

l: plan to murder Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Kishkumen planned to murder Helaman in order to destroy him. Helaman's servant learned of the plan through disguise and prevented it by killing Kishkumen.

l: the secret band of Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The band's secret plan was to murder, rob, and gain power, and the text identifies this as their secret plan and combination.

l: murder of Kishkumen, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: Helaman's servant stabbed Kishkumen even to the heart as they went toward the judgment-seat, and Kishkumen fell dead without a groan.

l: flight of Gadianton's band, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: When Gadianton learned that Kishkumen had not returned, he caused his band to follow him. They fled out of the land by a secret way into the wilderness and could not be found.

l: overthrow and near-destruction of the people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 2
s: The text states that Gadianton would prove the overthrow, almost the entire destruction, of the people of Nephi.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The people of Nephi experience contention, dissensions, wars, migration, and settlement throughout the land northward, followed by periods of peace, prosperity, and joy. The people build cities, temples, synagogues, and sanctuaries, while many Lamanites and people of Ammon also enter the land northward. The church of God grows through baptism unto repentance, but pride, persecution, and secret combinations arise among the people. Helaman governs righteously, dies in the fifty-third year of the reign of the judges, and is succeeded by his son Nephi.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The people of Nephi experience contention, dissensions, wars, migration, prosperity, peace, pride, and persecution. They keep many records, and many are eventually scattered, slain, or mixed with the Lamanites.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The Lamanites include people of Ammon who go into the land northward. Some Nephites are eventually mixed with the Lamanites and become called Lamanites.

l: church of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The church of God experiences great prosperity, with thousands joining and being baptized unto repentance. Pride enters the hearts of some who profess to belong to it, leading to persecution.

l: Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Gadianton the robber establishes secret combinations in the more settled parts of the land, but those at the head of government do not know of them.

l: Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Helaman fills the judgment-seat with justice and equity, keeps God's commandments, and prospers in the land. He has two sons, Nephi and Lehi, and dies in the fifty-third year of the reign of the judges.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Nephi is Helaman's eldest son. After Helaman dies, Nephi begins to reign in his stead and fills the judgment-seat with justice and equity.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Son of God, and those who believe on his name may enter the gate of heaven.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: God is shown as merciful to all who sincerely call upon his holy name. The people who yield their hearts unto God receive purification and sanctification.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The land of Zarahemla experiences continual rejoicing in the forty-ninth year, along with the regions round about possessed by the Nephites.

l: the land northward, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Many people migrate to the land northward, where they encounter large bodies of water and rivers and spread throughout the land. Because timber is scarce, they become expert in cement and build many cities and other structures.

l: kingdom of heaven, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The kingdom of heaven is described as the place where the souls of the faithful may sit with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and the holy fathers.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The word of God is described as quick and powerful, able to divide asunder the cunning, snares, and wiles of the devil and lead the man of Christ in a strait and narrow course.

l: the reign of the judges, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The reign of the judges includes years of contention, wars, prosperity, peace, pride, and the succession from Helaman to Nephi in the fifty-third year.

l: contentions, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Contention occurs among the people in the forty-sixth through forty-eighth years, then begins to cease in the latter end of the forty-eighth year. Continual peace is established in the forty-ninth year.

l: dissensions, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Dissensions arise among the people, especially during the forty-sixth year, and accompany contention and wars.

l: wars, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Wars and contentions occur among the people through the forty-eighth year, then begin to cease in a small degree.

l: migration to the land northward, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: An exceedingly great many people depart from Zarahemla and travel northward to inherit the land. They spread across the land and establish cities and settlements.

l: the secret band of Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Secret combinations established by Gadianton the robber remain in the more settled parts of the land because those at the head of government do not know about them.

l: baptism unto repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Thousands join the church and are baptized unto repentance during a period of great prosperity. Many souls, even tens of thousands, are baptized and united to the church of God.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Repentance accompanies the growth of the church, as people are baptized unto repentance and united to the church of God.

l: prosperity, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The church experiences exceedingly great prosperity in the forty-ninth year, bringing thousands into the church and causing even the high priests and teachers to be astonished.

l: peace, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Continual peace is established in the forty-ninth year and continues through the fiftieth year. Peace also marks the end of the fifty-second year, despite exceedingly great pride.

l: joy, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The people experience continual rejoicing, exceedingly great joy, and great joy during the forty-ninth and fiftieth years.

l: pride, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Pride causes little dissensions early in the unit and later enters the church through the hearts of people who profess to belong to it. It grows because of riches and prosperity and leads to persecution.

l: persecution, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: People lifted up in pride persecute many of their brethren. The more humble part of the people suffers great persecutions and affliction but grows stronger in humility and faith.

l: faith of Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: The humble people fast and pray often and become firmer in the faith of Christ. Their faith contributes to joy, consolation, purification, and sanctification.

l: death of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: Helaman dies in the fifty-third year of the reign of the judges, after governing with justice and equity and raising Nephi and Lehi.

l: succession of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 3
s: After Helaman's death, his eldest son Nephi begins to reign in his stead and takes the judgment-seat.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites suffered bloodshed, lost most of their lands to the Lamanites and dissenters from the Nephites, and later regained half their possessions under Moronihah after repenting. Their wickedness included pride, oppression, violence, disbelief, and violations of the laws of Mosiah and commandments of God, causing the Spirit of the Lord to withdraw and the Lord to cease preserving them by miraculous and matchless power. Nephi and Lehi preached and prophesied to the people of the Nephites, while Moronihah led the armies of Moronihah in defending and recovering Nephite lands. The Nephites recognized that their weakness, slaughter, loss, and fear resulted from their iniquity and failure to cleave unto the Lord their God.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites suffered bloodshed and were driven by the Lamanites into the land of Bountiful, losing almost all their lands. After repenting, they regained half of their possessions, but they could obtain no more land because the Lamanites were too numerous.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Lamanites were stirred up to anger by dissenters from the Nephites and obtained possession of the land of Zarahemla, the land southward, and other Nephite lands. They were more numerous than the Nephites and had strength equal to them man for man.

l: dissenters, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Dissenters from the Nephites went to the Lamanites and stirred them up to war against the Nephites. With the help of a numerous Lamanite army, they obtained the Nephites' possessions in the land southward.

l: Moronihah, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Moronihah preached to the people because of their iniquity and led the Nephites to regain half of their possessions after they repented. He later maintained the recovered lands when he could obtain no more possessions from the Lamanites.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Nephi, together with Lehi, preached and prophesied to the people concerning their iniquities and what would happen if they did not repent.

l: Lehi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Lehi, together with Nephi, preached and prophesied to the people concerning their iniquities and what would happen if they did not repent.

l: church of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The church of God included people involved in wickedness, and because of their iniquity it began to dwindle. Some who professed to belong to it denied the spirit of prophecy and the spirit of revelation.

l: the people of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The people of the Nephites were preached to by Moronihah, Nephi, and Lehi concerning their iniquities. They repented, began to prosper, and remembered the prophecies of Alma and the words of Mosiah.

l: armies of Moronihah, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The armies of Moronihah were driven into the land of Bountiful and fortified a line from the west sea to the east. They later regained many cities and half of the Nephites' possessions, then defended the recovered lands.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The land of Zarahemla was obtained by the Lamanites in the fifty-eighth year of the reign of the judges.

l: land of Bountiful, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites and the armies of Moronihah were driven into the land of Bountiful, where they fortified against the Lamanites.

l: land southward, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Dissenters from the Nephites, assisted by the Lamanites, obtained all the possession of the Nephites that was in the land southward.

l: war between the Nephites and Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The war began after dissenters stirred the Lamanites to anger against the Nephites. The Lamanites gained extensive lands, while the Nephites later recovered half of their possessions but could obtain no more.

l: slaughter of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites experienced great slaughter because of their wickedness and abomination, including pride, oppression, violence, and disbelief.

l: loss of the Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites' great loss occurred because of their wickedness and abomination. They lost possession of almost all their lands before repenting and regaining half of them.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites repented after preaching by Moronihah, Nephi, and Lehi, and as they repented they began to prosper. Their repentance enabled Moronihah to lead them to regain half of their possessions and lands.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: Wickedness and iniquity among the Nephites included pride, riches, oppression of the poor, withholding food and clothing, violence, mocking sacred things, denying prophecy and revelation, murder, plundering, lying, stealing, adultery, contention, and desertion to the Lamanites. Because of it, they were afflicted, smitten, driven before the Lamanites, and weakened.

l: spirit of prophecy, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites began to disbelieve in the spirit of prophecy, and some who professed to belong to the church of God denied it.

l: spirit of revelation, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites began to disbelieve in the spirit of revelation, and some who professed to belong to the church of God denied it.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Spirit of the Lord no longer preserved the Nephites and had withdrawn from them because it does not dwell in unholy temples.

l: laws of Mosiah, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites altered and trampled under their feet the laws of Mosiah, which contributed to their becoming a wicked people.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Nephites set at naught the commandments of God and recognized that this disobedience had contributed to their wickedness and weakness.

l: judgments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The judgments of God stared the Nephites in the face after the church dwindled and they became wicked and disbelieving.

l: miraculous and matchless power of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 4
s: The Lord ceased to preserve the Nephites by his miraculous and matchless power because they had fallen into unbelief and awful wickedness.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi gives up the judgment-seat to Cezoram and, with Lehi, preaches the word of God after remembering Helaman’s teachings about commandments, repentance, Jesus Christ, and the rock of the Redeemer. Nephi and Lehi preach among the Nephites and Lamanites, leading many dissenters and thousands of Lamanites to confess their sins and receive baptism unto repentance. After Nephi and Lehi are imprisoned, God manifests power through fire, earthquakes, darkness, and a voice, and the Lamanites repent, receive the Holy Spirit of God, and see angels of God. About three hundred people testify of these things, and many Lamanites lay down their weapons of war, hatred, and the traditions of their fathers, yielding their lands to the Nephites.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi gives up the judgment-seat to Cezoram because of the iniquity of the people and spends the remainder of his days preaching the word of God with Lehi. He preaches to the Nephites and Lamanites, is imprisoned with Lehi, and is encircled by fire without being burned.

l: Lehi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Lehi joins Nephi in preaching the word of God among the Nephites and Lamanites. He is imprisoned with Nephi and is encircled by fire without being burned; his face shines as the face of an angel.

l: Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Helaman taught Nephi and Lehi to remember the commandments of God, the works of their first parents, repentance, Jesus Christ, and the rock of the Redeemer.

l: Aminadab, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Aminadab, a Nephite by birth and former member of the church of God, identifies Nephi and Lehi as conversing with the angels of God. He tells the Lamanites to repent and cry unto the voice until they have faith in Christ.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: God shows power through fire, earthquakes, darkness, and a voice that commands the people to repent and stop seeking to destroy His servants. He sends the Holy Spirit of God and angels of God to minister to those who repent and have faith.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the Son of God, the Redeemer, and the only way by which people can be saved. Faith in Him brings peace and is associated with repentance and salvation.

l: angels of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The angels of God are identified as the beings with whom Nephi and Lehi converse. Angels come down from heaven and minister to about three hundred souls.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Nephites have laws and governments established by the voice of the people, but their laws have become corrupted because those choosing evil are more numerous. Nephi and Lehi preach among them, and repentant Lamanites yield lands to them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Lamanites hear Nephi and Lehi preach, and eight thousand in Zarahemla and the surrounding area are baptized unto repentance. Lamanites imprison Nephi and Lehi, later repent, receive spiritual manifestations, and many lay down their weapons, hatred, and traditions before yielding lands to the Nephites.

l: dissenters, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Dissenters who had gone over from the Nephites are confounded by the preaching of Nephi and Lehi; many confess their sins, receive baptism unto repentance, and return to the Nephites to repair the wrongs they had done.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Helaman teaches Nephi and Lehi to remember and keep the commandments of God. Nephi and Lehi remember them and go forth keeping them while teaching the word of God.

l: word of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi and Lehi take upon themselves to preach the word of God among the people of Nephi and the Lamanites. Their preaching is accompanied by great power and authority.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Repentance is taught as the condition connected with the power of the Redeemer and salvation of souls. The voice repeatedly commands the Lamanites to repent, and Aminadab teaches them to repent and cry unto the voice.

l: eternal life, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Helaman teaches that doing good without boasting lays up a treasure in heaven and may bring the precious gift of eternal life.

l: atoning blood of Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Helaman teaches that there is no other way or means whereby people can be saved except through the atoning blood of Jesus Christ, who comes to redeem the world.

l: rock of our Redeemer, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Helaman teaches that people must build their foundation upon the rock of their Redeemer, Christ, the Son of God. Those built upon this sure foundation cannot fall despite the devil’s storms.

l: prison, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi and Lehi are cast into the same prison in which Ammon and his brethren were cast by the servants of Limhi. The prison shakes, is surrounded by fire, and remains standing during the manifestations.

l: pillar of fire, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: A pillar of fire encircles Nephi and Lehi and prevents the Lamanites from laying hands on them. After the cloud of darkness is removed, every soul is encircled by a pillar of fire, which does not harm them or the prison walls.

l: cloud of darkness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: A cloud of darkness overshadows the people in the prison, causing fear and preventing the Lamanites from fleeing. It is dispersed after they repent and cry unto the voice.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Holy Spirit of God comes down from heaven and enters the hearts of the people after the cloud of darkness is dispersed. They are filled as if with fire and speak marvelous words.

l: voice, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: A voice from above the cloud of darkness commands the people to repent and stop seeking to destroy God’s servants. It is a still, mild voice that pierces to the soul, and later speaks peace because of their faith in the Well Beloved.

l: earthquake, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The earth shakes exceedingly when Nephi and Lehi speak, when the voice commands repentance, and when marvelous words are spoken. The shaking occurs repeatedly while the prison walls tremble but do not fall.

l: preaching, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi and Lehi preach with great power and authority from city to city among the Nephites and Lamanites. Their preaching confounds dissenters and convinces many Lamanites of the wickedness of their fathers’ traditions.

l: baptism unto repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Many dissenters confess their sins and are baptized unto repentance before returning to the Nephites. Eight thousand Lamanites in Zarahemla and the surrounding area are also baptized unto repentance.

l: conversion of many of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The preaching and spiritual manifestations involving Nephi and Lehi convince many Lamanites. Those convinced lay down their weapons, hatred, and traditions, and yield their lands to the Nephites.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: Nephi and Lehi preach in the land of Zarahemla, where eight thousand Lamanites and those round about are baptized unto repentance.

l: weapons of war, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: As many Lamanites as are convinced lay down their weapons of war along with their hatred and the traditions of their fathers.

l: traditions of their fathers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 5
s: The Lamanites are convinced of the wickedness of the traditions of their fathers. Many lay down these traditions after repenting and receiving spiritual evidences.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Lamanites become largely righteous through firmness in the faith, while many Nephites grow hardened, wicked, and attached to riches. The people of the church rejoice in the Lamanites’ conversion, and Lamanites preach faith and repentance among the Nephites. Peace and prosperity end when Gadianton’s band spreads secret murders, robberies, oaths, and covenants among the Nephites, leading them to control the government and oppress the poor and humble. The Spirit of the Lord withdraws from the Nephites but is poured out upon the Lamanites, who destroy the robbers among them.

l: Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Lamanites become, for the most part, a righteous people whose righteousness exceeds that of the Nephites because of their firmness and steadiness in the faith. They preach faith and repentance, travel freely among the Nephites, grow rich, and destroy Gadianton’s band from among them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Many Nephites become hardened, impenitent, and grossly wicked. They join Gadianton’s bands, commit murders and other wickedness, set their hearts upon riches, gain control of the government, oppress the poor and humble, and dwindle in unbelief.

l: the people of the church, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The people of the church have great joy because of the conversion of the Lamanites and fellowship and rejoice with one another.

l: church of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The church of God is established among the Lamanites, contributing to the joy of the people of the church.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: God is the one whose word, preaching, and commandments the wicked Nephites reject and trample under their feet. The humble followers of God seek to follow him.

l: the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Lord blesses the people with riches and later withdraws his Spirit from the Nephites because of their wickedness and hardness of heart. He pours out his Spirit upon the Lamanites because of their willingness to believe his words.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Spirit of the Lord begins to withdraw from the Nephites because of their wickedness and hard hearts, while it is poured out upon the Lamanites because of their easiness and willingness to believe.

l: Kishkumen, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Kishkumen helps form the band of murderers and plunderers with Gadianton. He and Gadianton give laws governing the band’s secret wickedness.

l: Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Gadianton helps form the band of murderers and plunderers and gives them secret laws. Satan puts secret oaths, covenants, and works of darkness into Gadianton’s heart.

l: Satan, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Satan stirs up the hearts of many Nephites to unite with bands of robbers and enter their covenants. He is described as the author of sin who carries on secret murder and passes wicked plots, oaths, covenants, and plans from generation to generation.

l: secret band of robbers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Gadianton’s band consists of murderers and plunderers who use covenants, secret signs, and secret words to protect one another. It spreads among the Nephites, seduces many, obtains control of the government, and oppresses the poor and humble.

l: Gadianton’s robbers and murderers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Gadianton’s robbers and murderers murder Cezoram and his son while they are in the judgment-seat and are not found. The Lamanites hunt and destroy the band among themselves, while the Nephites build it up.

l: conversion of many of the Lamanites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The conversion of the Lamanites brings great joy to the people of the church. Converted Lamanites declare its manner to the Nephites and exhort them to faith and repentance.

l: faith, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Lamanites become righteous through firmness and steadiness in the faith. They preach faith to the Nephites and are willing to believe God’s words.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Lamanites preach repentance to the Nephites and bring many down into humility as humble followers of God and the Lamb.

l: righteousness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The righteousness of the Lamanites exceeds that of the Nephites because of their firmness and steadiness in the faith. The Nephites turn from righteousness and trample God’s commandments.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Wickedness increases among the Nephites through riches, secret murders, robbery, plunder, and secret combinations. The Nephites become exceedingly wicked, while the Lamanites grow in knowledge of God and uprightness.

l: peace, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: There is peace throughout the land while the Nephites and Lamanites travel, trade, and prosper freely. This period of peace ends as the people grow wicked and secret murders begin.

l: riches, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Nephites and Lamanites become exceedingly rich through gold, silver, precious metals, abundant grain, flocks, herds, and cloth. The Nephites later set their hearts upon riches and seek gain to elevate themselves above one another.

l: murder, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Secret murders are committed by Gadianton’s bands to obtain gain. The Nephites join in secret murders and combinations, and Cezoram and his son are murdered in the judgment-seat.

l: secret oaths and covenants, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: Secret oaths and covenants bind members of the robbers’ bands to protect one another from punishment for murder, plunder, stealing, and other wickedness. Alma had commanded that these oaths and covenants not be revealed because they could bring the people to destruction.

l: the commandments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The more part of the Nephites turn away from and trample under their feet the commandments of God. They replace obedience with their own ways and idols of gold and silver.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 6
s: The Nephites become ripened for an everlasting destruction because of their wickedness and oppression. The secret oaths and covenants are identified as a means of bringing the people down to destruction.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned to the land of Zarahemla after the people in the land northward rejected his preaching and prophecies. He mourned the wickedness of the Nephites, including the Gadianton robbers’ control of judgment-seats and government. Nephi called the people to repentance, warning that their cities, lands, and strength would be taken away if they did not repent. He testified that the Lord God had revealed these things to him and that the Nephites would be destroyed unless they repented.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi, the son of Helaman, returned to the land of Zarahemla after preaching and prophesying among the people in the land northward, who rejected his words. He mourned over the wickedness of the Nephites, called them to repentance, and testified of the judgments that would come upon them.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The Nephites had become greatly wicked, setting their hearts on riches and permitting murder, plunder, theft, false witness, and other iniquity. They were warned that their cities and lands would be taken from them and that they would be destroyed unless they repented.

l: Gadianton’s robbers and murderers, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The Gadianton robbers filled the judgment-seats and usurped the power and authority of the land. They laid aside the commandments of God, did no justice, and used their offices for gain, glory, and wicked acts.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The Lord God made known to Nephi that the judgments he proclaimed were true. He would not show his strength to the wicked unless they repented and hearkened to his words.

l: land of Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The land of Zarahemla was where Nephi returned and where he mourned upon a tower in his garden. It contained a people whose wickedness had become great.

l: Zarahemla, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Zarahemla was the city where Nephi's tower and garden were located. Nephi warned that Zarahemla and the surrounding great cities would be taken away if the people did not repent.

l: wickedness, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The people's wickedness had become severe within a short time, involving pride, riches, iniquity, and the influence of the Gadianton robbers. It caused Nephi great sorrow and led him to warn the people of destruction.

l: Nephi's mourning, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Nephi's mourning arose from the exceeding sorrow of his heart because of the people's iniquities. He poured out his soul unto God upon a tower, causing multitudes to gather and prompting him to preach repentance.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: Repentance was repeatedly commanded as the way for the people to turn unto the Lord and avoid destruction. Those who did not repent would lose their cities and lands and be destroyed, while the Lord would show strength to those who repented and hearkened to his words.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 7
s: The destruction of the Nephites was foretold as the consequence of refusing to repent. Their cities and lands would be taken from them, and they would be destroyed from off the face of the earth.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Nephi condemns the judges and their corrupt law, secret works of darkness, murders, fornication, and wickedness, while some of the people defend him as a prophet. He teaches that Moses, Abraham, and the holy prophets testified of the Messiah, the coming of Christ, and redemption. Nephi warns that the judgments will come upon the people unless they repent, and reveals that their judge has been murdered by his brother, who seeks the judgment-seat. The judges and the murderer belong to the secret band of Gadianton, whose author is Gadianton and the evil one.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Nephi speaks plainly against the judges, their corrupt law, and their secret works of darkness. He testifies of the judgments that will come upon the people unless they repent and reveals that the judge has been murdered.

l: the judges, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The judges belong to the secret band of Gadianton and become angry with Nephi. They accuse him before the people but do not lay hands on him because they fear the people.

l: the secret band of Gadianton, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The secret band of Gadianton includes the judges and the murderer of the judge. Its author is Gadianton and the evil one who seeks to destroy the souls of men.

l: Nephites, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The people are stirred to anger against Nephi, but some defend him and testify that his warnings will come to pass unless they repent. Their murders, fornication, and wickedness bring them toward destruction.

l: Moses, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Moses was given power by God to divide the waters of the Red Sea. He testified concerning the coming of the Messiah and lifted up the brazen serpent as a likeness of the Son of God.

l: Jesus Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The Messiah was testified of by Moses and the fathers. He is represented by the serpent lifted up in the wilderness.

l: Abraham, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Abraham saw of the coming of the Son of God, was filled with gladness, and rejoiced. He was among those who knew of these things.

l: the holy prophets, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The holy prophets testified of the Messiah and the coming of Christ. They include prophets from the days of Moses and Abraham through the days of Nephi.

l: Jerusalem, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Jerusalem was destroyed according to the words of Jeremiah. Lehi was driven out of Jerusalem because he testified of the coming of Christ.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: God gave Moses power over the waters of the Red Sea and gave power to others by his order. He is called the holy God, whom the people rejected and against whom they rebelled.

l: secret work of murder and robbery, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Nephi speaks plainly to the judges concerning their secret works of darkness. The judges become angry because he exposes them.

l: the law, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Nephi speaks concerning the corruptness of the law. The judges accuse him of reviling against the people and their law.

l: judgments of God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Nephi testifies that the judgments will come upon the people unless they repent. He says they are now at the people's doors.

l: the coming of Christ, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The fathers and almost all the prophets testified of the coming of Christ. They looked forward to it and rejoiced in the day that is to come.

l: redemption, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Redemption was to come to the people through the Son of God. Abraham and others knew of these things, and the people were shown them many thousand years before his coming.

l: eternal life, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: Those who look upon the Son of God with faith and a contrite spirit may live unto eternal life.

l: repentance, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The people are warned that the judgments and destruction will come upon them unless they repent. Some people say Nephi is a good man because his warnings will come to pass if they do not repent.

l: the destruction of Jerusalem, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The destruction of Jerusalem occurred according to Jeremiah's words. Nephi uses it as evidence that the Son of God will come according to prophecy.

l: murder of Pahoran, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The judge is murdered and lies in his blood. He is murdered by his brother, who seeks to sit in the judgment-seat.

l: the day of judgment, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The people are heaping up wrath against the day of judgment instead of laying up treasures in heaven. Their murders, fornication, and wickedness are ripening them for destruction.

l: destruction, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 8
s: The people are ripening because of their murders, fornication, and wickedness for everlasting destruction. Nephi warns that it will come soon unless they repent.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Nephi’s prophecy that the chief judge would be dead is confirmed when five men find Seezoram murdered at the judgment-seat. The people mistake the five men for the murderers and imprison them, but the judges later release them after hearing their account. Nephi directs the people to question Seantum, Seezoram’s brother, and his guilt is exposed when he confesses to the murder. Some Nephites believe Nephi is a prophet, while others call him a god because he knows hidden things.

l: Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Nephi is accused by the judges of conspiring to murder Seezoram, but he denies the accusation and gives instructions that reveal Seantum as the murderer. He is bound and questioned, then released after Seantum confesses.

l: God, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: God is invoked as the source of Nephi’s knowledge and power. The people believe Nephi’s signs and testimony show that he is sent by God, and some call him a god.

l: Seezoram, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Seezoram is the chief judge who is found dead at the judgment-seat. The text reveals that his brother Seantum murdered him.

l: Seantum, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Seantum is Seezoram’s brother and the murderer of Seezoram. When questioned as Nephi predicted, he initially denies the murder but is exposed by blood on his cloak and eventually confesses.

l: five men, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The five men run to the judgment-seat to test Nephi’s prophecy and find Seezoram dead. The people mistakenly imprison them as murderers, but they are later released after their account is confirmed.

l: people of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The people gather at the judgment-seat, mistake the five men for murderers, and mourn and fast at Seezoram’s burial. Some later believe Nephi is a prophet, while others call him a god.

l: the judges, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The judges at the garden of Nephi attend Seezoram’s burial, question the five men, and accuse Nephi of arranging the murder. They bring Nephi before the multitude and later learn through Seantum’s confession that Nephi was not the murderer.

l: judgment-seat, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The judgment-seat is where Seezoram is found lying dead in his blood. The people gather there and wrongly identify the five men as his murderers.

l: garden of Nephi, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The garden of Nephi is where the judges hear Nephi’s words before gathering at the burial of the chief judge.

l: prison, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The five men are cast into prison after the people mistakenly accuse them of murdering Seezoram. They are later released on the day of the burial, and their imprisonment contributes to their conversion.

l: murder of Seezoram, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The murder of Seezoram is committed by his brother Seantum, who stabs him under a garb of secrecy. Nephi predicts how Seantum’s guilt will be exposed, and Seantum confesses.

l: burial of the chief judge, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: The people assemble to mourn and fast at the burial of the slain chief judge, Seezoram. The judges and the five men are involved in events surrounding the burial, and the five men are released that day.

l: Nephi's prophecy, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 9
s: Nephi’s prophecy that the chief judge would be dead is confirmed when the five men find Seezoram’s body. Nephi also prophesies the questioning, signs of guilt, and confession of Seantum, and these details occur as he described.

l: The Book of Helaman, The Book of Helaman, Chapter 10
s: Nephi is left alone after a division among the people and ponders the wickedness of the people of the Nephites. God tells Nephi that he has served faithfully and grants him power over the people, including power connected with sealing, loosening, and declaring judgments. Nephi declares that the people must repent or be smitten unto destruction, but they harden their hearts, revile him, and try to imprison him. The Spirit conveys Nephi away, and afterward contentions arise until the people begin slaying one another with the sword.
